findings.title: Invalid UTF-8 in a config file silently alters its patterns
findings.description: The default config reader in `main` decodes the file with `readFileSync(path, 'utf8')`, which replaces each invalid byte sequence with U+FFFD. `parseConfig` and `compileIgnorePattern` then validate and compile the replaced text, so a pattern that contained invalid bytes is accepted and matched in a different form than the one written in the file. A maintainer with a stray byte in a pattern gets no error and no hint that the regex in use differs from the file, and no test covers this path.

citations.citation: Validate raw parser fields before normalization

evidence.explanation: The reader decodes with a replacing UTF-8 decoder before `parseConfig` sees any text, so the validation cannot detect that bytes were altered. This is normalization ahead of validation that lets input invalid in the file pass validation, which the parser rule forbids. The author's notes list this case as untested.

findings.title: A config path can forge error lines
findings.description: `loadConfig` JSON-encodes the path but appends the file reader's error message to stderr without escaping control characters. If a nonexistent `--config` path contains a newline, the read failure can produce additional apparent error lines instead of the intended single-line diagnostic.

location.code_snippet:
+    const detail = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
+    return { error: `error: cannot read config ${JSON.stringify(configPath)}: ${detail}\n` };

evidence.explanation: The option loop accepts the supplied path verbatim. The default reader passes it to `readFileSync`; on failure, `loadConfig` appends the exception message without escaping it and the command writes that result to stderr. The existing one-line test covers only ordinary fixture paths.
